messages:
sarah.p: FYI - getting multiple p95/p99 latency escalations since last night's maintenance window (03:12 UTC). CS ticket #CS-4712 and internal dashboards show p95 from ~350ms -> 1.8-2.5s for text-generation endpoints in us-west-2. Customers reporting timeouts at 10s.
mike.r: Which infra change was in that window? I think we pushed a host kernel + nvidia driver combo to the canaries around 03:05.
sarah.p: Right — the change rolled to canary pool at 03:05 and to prod at 03:10. Kernel bump 5.15.0-89 -> 5.15.0-91 and driver 535.xx -> 535.86 (packaged build). Also a small NVMe firmware refresh on a subset of hosts (non-disruptive according to vendor notes).
julia.l: I'm pulling traces now. Observing increased tail on nvme io wait on affected hosts. iostat shows %util on nvme0 goes 15% -> 88% under same workload. p99 correlates almost perfectly with NVMe queue depth spikes.
tim.oncall: ops-bot flagged some Xid errors right after 03:12 on a few machines: "NVRM: Xid 31: Uncorrectable ECC error" then kernel logged NVMe timeouts. Posting logs.
ops-bot: [automated] host=i-0a1234: dmesg excerpt:
  "nvme 0000:3a:00.0: I/O 12345 QID 0 timeout, status=0x2
   nvme: aborting command (status=0x2)
   NVRM: Xid (31): Uncorrectable ECC error on GPU 0"
leo.k: Repro steps I'm running locally: run loadgen against /v1/generate with model=redwood/llama2-13b, seq=2048, batch=1, concurrency=40. Hitting p99 ~2s on hosts with new driver. Rolling the same test on older-driver hosts yields p99 ~360ms.
mike.r: So we have co-occurrence of (driver upgrade + kernel bump + NVMe firmware). Which is causal? Any host that has driver+kernel but not firmware shows the issue?
julia.l: I compared three canaries: A (old driver/kernel, old NVMe fw) -> clean. B (new driver + old fw) -> noisy but lower p99 than full set. C (new driver + new fw) -> worst. So strongest signal is driver+fw combo, but there may be an interrupt handling regression in kernel as well.
cs-escalations: Customer A sent a flame: "sudden latency spike breaking product UI, please escalate". They've asked for ETA and mitigation.
sarah.p: Immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) Rollback driver on affected pools to previous known-good (510-series). 2) Temporarily route critical customers to dedicated hosts that we haven't patched. 3) Enable request-level fallback: lower batch sizes and reduce concurrency for affected routes. Who can do the rollback?
tim.oncall: I can scrub and roll back canaries now. Plan: revert driver package to 510.79 and hold kernel at 5.15.0-89 for a small cohort, validate p95 across canaries, then expand. Will coordinate with deploy-bot.
mike.r: Also recommend disabling NVMe firmware update rollout until we confirm it isn't amplifying the issue. Ops: freeze firmware changes.
ops-bot: [automated] Rolling back driver on group=canary-1 -> started. Hosts: i-0a1234,i-0b2345,i-0c3456. ETA ~16m.
leo.k: Quick note: in some reproduction runs I saw a CPU steal / softirq backlog spike that seems tied to kernel's handling of NVMe IRQs when driver hits Xid. Could be causing scheduler stalls that increase tail latency for inference processes.
julia.l: Will add perf stat snapshot after rollback and compare softirq and irq counts. Also collecting GPU metrics: nvml shows GPU utilization steady but GPU kernel queues blocked for tens to hundreds ms when NVMe stalls occur.
tim.oncall: Rollback complete on canary-1. Preliminary metrics: p95 down from 1.9s -> 380ms, p99 down to ~780ms. Still above baseline but much better. Starting staged rollback to prod-1 group next.
mike.r: Good. While we rollback, implement a short-term traffic policy: route heavy RLHF workloads and long-seq batches to the older pool. Add a temporary circuit-breaker at 1.5s to avoid client-visible timeouts.
cs-escalations: Sent customer A follow-up: "we've identified a perf regression tied to an infra upgrade; we've routed you to a stable pool and are rolling back across the fleet. ETA ~2 hours. Apologies." They acknowledged.
sarah.p: After prod rollback completes we should validate: 1) run synthetic across regions, 2) run customer repro load, 3) check for residual p99 on fallback hosts. Also open a ticket with driver vendor + GPU vendor with logs (Xid messages + nvme timeout traces) and attach perf profiles.
julia.l: Action items I took: - collected perf+ftrace dumps for 6 affected hosts -> /artifacts/CS-4712/pft-1812345678-1.tar.gz - iostat + nvme-cli logs captured - core dumps and NVRM logs archived.
leo.k: I'll prepare a minimal repro harness that toggles NVMe stress with inference load to reproduce in lab. If firmware amplifies it, we can reproduce without firmware by simulating NVMe latency.
mike.r: Long term we need: - tighter preflight for combined driver+kernel+fw rollouts (run NVMe stress + high-concurrency inference in CI) - add test that simulates Xid/driver error path to ensure it doesn't stall host - make request routing tolerant to short host stalls (faster failover).
tim.oncall: Scheduling 1-hour incident follow-up at 16:00 UTC with eng-runtime, eng-infra, and CS. I'll put notes in calendar and include rollback timeline and metrics.
sarah.p: Thanks everyone. Final note: keep the firmware rollout paused and don't reapply driver 535 until vendor provides a fix or we validate in lab. I'll update the incident page and CS ticket.

mike.r: Postmortem items assigned: julia -> diagnostics + perf graphs, leo -> lab repro, tim -> rollout automation update, sarah -> vendor outreach + customer comms.

ops-bot: [automated] Incident timeline entry created: INCIDENT-2026-1113-01, severity: high, owners: eng-sre.

cs-escalations: Customer A confirmed they see normal latency after being routed. Will keep ticket open until full fleet stable.

sarah.p: Closing loop: prod rollback finished at 05:30 UTC. Final fleet p95 ~370ms, p99 ~820ms (slightly above baseline p99 ~620ms). We'll track for 24h and escalate to vendor if we see recurrence.
